Key Theorists: Hofstede, Triandis, Markus & Kitayama, Kwame Gyekye, Kwasi Wiredu
Psychological Core Definition: Interdependent self-construal prioritizing in-group goals, shared fate, and relational duties over atomistic self-interest.
Akan / Twi Manifestation: Moderate Communalism ('Onipa nua ne nipa'); individual identity realized through the matriclan (Abusua) and mutual labor (Nnoboa). Individualism (Pɛsɛmenkominya, Ahopɛ) is pathologized.
Key Linguistic Markers: 1st-person plural shifts (yɛn), broad kinship terms (onua, wofa), pejorative compounds for selfishness (pɛsɛmenkominya, ahomasoɔ).

Key Theorists: Hofstede, Schwartz (Hierarchy vs. Egalitarianism), Brown & Levinson
Psychological Core Definition: Acceptance and institutionalization of power asymmetry, age-graded deference, and social stratification.
Akan / Twi Manifestation: Sacred chieftaincy (Ahemfo), Queenmothers (Ahemmaa), elder councils (Mpanyinfoɔ), and ancestral hierarchy (Nsamanfoɔ). Respect (Obuo) and humility (Ahobraseɛ) are mandatory virtues.
Key Linguistic Markers: Sacred honorifics (Nana, Opanyin), royal linguistic mediation (Okyeame), clan-graded response tokens (Yaa Agya, Yaa Ena), physical deference (Nkotodwe-gu).

Psychological Core Definition: Strength of social norms and strictness of sanctions against deviant behavior (Tight = strong norms/sanctions; Loose = tolerant).
Akan / Twi Manifestation: High tightness around sacred taboos (Akyiwadeɛ), taboo calendar days (Dabɔne), purification rites (Asubɔ/Dwira), and moral character requirements (Suban pa).
Key Linguistic Markers: Taboo lexica (akyiwadeɛ, dabɔne), sanction terms (musuo, asotwe), deviance descriptors (ti-ɛden, asoɔden).

Psychological Core Definition: Social self-esteem, public image, and collective reputation managed through honor preservation and shame avoidance.
Akan / Twi Manifestation: Bright face / glory (Animuonyam) as highest social credit; shame (Fɛre) as supreme internal and communal regulator; public disgrace (Anim-guaseɛ) seen as worse than physical death.
Key Linguistic Markers: Face compounds (anim-uonyam = shining face; anim-tia = diminished face; anim-guaseɛ = fallen face; fɛre = shame).

Psychological Core Definition: Information is deeply embedded in context, relational status, and implicit shared codes rather than explicit literal statements.
Akan / Twi Manifestation: Extensive use of proverbs (Mmɛ), metaphorical speech (Kasakoa), royal spokesperson mediation (Okyeame), and deliberate circumlocution to preserve face and status.
Key Linguistic Markers: Proverb markers (wɔbɔ no bɛ), indirect metaphor (kasakoa), conflict mitigation terms (kasa bɔkɔɔ), avoidance of raw blunt speech (kasa-mprɔprɔ).

Key Theorists: Kwame Gyekye, Kwasi Wiredu, Kofi Asare Opoku
Psychological Core Definition: Cosmological view where selfhood is composed of divine soul, spiritual temperament, physical lineage blood, and ancestor communion.
Akan / Twi Manifestation: Tripartite personhood: Divine Soul (Okra), Character/Personality spirit (Sunsum), and Matrilineal blood (Mogya) embedded within ancestral watchful protection (Nsamanfoɔ).
Key Linguistic Markers: Cosmological terms (Okra, Sunsum, Mogya, Ntɔro, Nsamanfoɔ, Nyamesuro).
